channel.title: NodeDR Field Notes
channel.description: Source-linked technology incident reporting and practical continuity guides for small businesses.

item.title: When One Cloud Region Slows Down, a Restaurant Still Has Tables to Serve
item.description: Google Cloud reported a six-hour, ten-minute disruption affecting services in europe-west2. The practical question for a restaurant is what must keep working when a remote dependency cannot.

item.title: Pharmacy Continuity Starts with Knowing Where the Database Lives
item.description: A cloud-region incident is a useful prompt for pharmacies to map which parts of billing, inventory, and patient history are local and which rely on a provider.

item.title: A Shop Checkout Should Have a Plan for the Network It Depends On
item.description: The October 2026 Google Cloud disruption is a prompt to distinguish a cloud dashboard from the local checkout path a shop needs at the counter.

item.title: The AWS Outage Lesson: Count Dependencies, Not Just Servers
item.description: AWS’s post-event summary explains how a DynamoDB DNS race condition in US-EAST-1 was followed by separate load-balancer and EC2 launch impacts, with different recovery times.

item.title: The Outage After the Outage: Can You Still Rebuild Your Software?
item.description: Docker reported that its October 2025 services were affected by the AWS US-EAST-1 event. It shows why recovery depends on deployment artifacts as well as running servers.

item.title: Remote Access Is a Convenience; the Restaurant LAN Is the Fallback
item.description: Cloudflare’s November 2025 postmortem described a global failure to deliver core network traffic. For a restaurant system, a tunnel can help remote access but should not be confused with the local service.

item.title: A CDN Is Part of the Product When the Login Page Needs It
item.description: Microsoft’s Azure status history documented Front Door and CDN connectivity issues across multiple regions in October 2025. Edge services can become a user-facing dependency even when application servers are healthy.

item.title: Self-Hosting Is Not a Backup Strategy
item.description: IDC Frontier reported a ransomware incident affecting part of its cloud service in October 2026 and described impact to 495 organizations. Its later update noted that snapshot availability differed among customers.

item.title: The Credential That Opens a Development Cloud Can Expose More Than Code
item.description: Nikkei disclosed in October 2026 that an unauthorized party accessed a cloud service used for system development; reporting described 1.83 million records in the incident.

item.title: An AI SDK Is Still Production Software With Supply-Chain Risk
item.description: CERT-In warned on 23 October 2026 of a LiteLLM package and container compromise. Microsoft’s analysis described malicious Python startup files in the affected release.

item.title: Why “We Never Imported That Library” Is Not a Complete Defense
item.description: In the October 2026 LiteLLM incident, Microsoft reported that affected Python package files could execute during interpreter startup, rather than waiting for an explicit import.

item.title: When a Critical Workflow Lives in One Vendor’s Login Screen
item.description: Instructure documented unauthorized Canvas activity in April and May 2026, with the service temporarily placed in maintenance mode during containment. The outage landed during a high-stakes academic period for some users.

item.title: The CareCloud Incident: Availability, Access, and Data Boundaries
item.description: CareCloud’s March 2026 SEC filing describes an eight-hour disruption affecting access to one of six EHR environments. It does not state in that filing that patient data was exfiltrated.

item.title: A Phone Call Can Be an Attack Path Around a Strong Firewall
item.description: Abbott said a vishing incident affected limited internal systems and that some files contained personal or health information; the company reported no impact to patient-facing operations.

item.title: A Security Incident Is Also a Test of Your Data Boundaries
item.description: Medtronic reported in 2026 that a cyber incident had affected some corporate IT systems and that it was contacting people whose information might have been impacted.

item.title: The Pharmacy Counter and the Claims Network Are Not the Same System
item.description: The 2024 Change Healthcare cyberattack disrupted claims and payment operations across the US health system. HHS described monitoring effects on access to care and concern for smaller practices.

item.title: One Malicious npm Package Can Reach Far Beyond the App That Uses It
item.description: Singapore’s Cyber Security Agency describes the 2025 Shai-Hulud campaign, in which compromised npm packages could search developer systems for credentials and propagate through package releases.

item.title: The Maintainer Account Is Part of the Software You Depend On
item.description: TanStack published a postmortem in May 2026 about a compromised npm release. Its account of the incident is a useful reminder that package publishing credentials can matter as much as source code review.

item.title: A Tunnel Adds Reach—and Another Dependency to Your Diagram
item.description: Cloudflare’s August 2025 incident report described congestion on links between Cloudflare and AWS US-EAST-1 during a traffic surge. The failure crossed a provider boundary rather than fitting one simple “cloud down” label.

item.title: A Region Can Be Healthy on the Dashboard and Still Be Your Single Point of Failure
item.description: Google Cloud’s 1 September 2026 report describes network degradation in parts of us-central1-b and us-central1-f after fiber was disconnected during scheduled maintenance. The event lasted 4 hours and 11 minutes; impacts varied by product and zone.
